elements.element: Customer (IBM) may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "IBM may, without MSL's consent and upon written notice to MSL, assign or transfer this Agreement ... to any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with IBM"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to any successor by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of the assets of the IBM business to which this Agreement relates"

elements.element: Vendor (MSL) may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM."

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor (absolute bar)
elements.evidence: No competitor bar appears; the only competitor reference is the termination trigger "acquired by an entity that competes directly with IBM, in which case IBM may terminate."

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: trigger narrowed to "substantially all of the shares or assets of MSL are acquired by an entity that competes directly with IBM, in which case IBM may terminate"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors (Vendor side included) with written notice
elements.evidence: only IBM gets the notice-based right; "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM."

elements.element: Customer right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: "IBM may, without MSL's consent and upon written notice to MSL, assign or transfer this Agreement"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed"

offending_extra_words: of the IBM business to which this Agreement relates
in which case IBM may terminate
reasons: Preferred level incomplete: the redline never bars MSL from assigning to an IBM competitor, which is an express preferred requirement; the reasonableness standard and the affiliate/successor carve-out do not substitute for that absolute prohibition.
Fallback level is also incomplete because the successor-assignment right is one-way (IBM only); MSL still needs consent for any successor assignment, so there is no mutual notice-based right.

Minimality fails: operation 1 rewrites a 22-word sentence into roughly 100 words (official gate: ratio 4.55 and changed-character ratio 0.765), where a short inserted carve-out sentence plus a five-word reasonableness insertion would suffice.

Unnecessary additions include the boilerplate lead-in "Except as expressly provided below", "in whole or in part", and the narrowing qualifier "of the IBM business to which this Agreement relates", which needlessly limits our own assignment right.

Operation 2 adds "in which case IBM may terminate" inside an enumerated trigger list where deleting the mutual reference ("of MSL ... with IBM") alone achieves the objective, adding an operative remedy statement beyond the minimal fix.
Unrelated commercial terms and the MSL Related Company consent mechanic remain intact, so intent is preserved, but the level target is not achieved.
